ASTRA CARE — Astronaut Health Monitoring & Self-Assessment System

ASTRA CARE is an offline-first, NASA-inspired astronaut health monitoring and self-assessment platform designed for long-duration space missions, including missions to Mars and the Moon.

The system enables astronauts to record vital health indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, sleep, mood, stress, and symptoms. It compares observations against personalized demonstration baselines, visualizes health trends, and provides explainable, non-diagnostic assessments to help astronauts better understand their health.

A key innovation is its offline-first medical reporting system, which allows astronauts to store health records locally, generate structured reports, and queue them for transmission when communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable. Once connectivity is restored, reports can be delivered to a simulated ground medical team with verified acknowledgements.

### Key Features
- Astronaut health monitoring and daily check-ins
- Health trend visualization and baseline comparison
- Explainable health assessments and educational guidance
- Offline-first data storage
- Delayed communication simulation
- Secure report integrity verification using SHA-256
- Structured medical reports and ground acknowledgement tracking
- Cross-platform web and mobile application
details:
ASTRA CARE — Autonomous Astronaut Health Monitoring & Self-Assessment System

ASTRA CARE is an offline-first, cross-platform health monitoring and self-assessment application designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions, particularly when communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable.

The Problem

Extended space missions expose astronauts to microgravity, radiation, isolation, and other health risks. During missions to Mars, communication delays make immediate consultation with medical professionals difficult. Astronauts need an accessible way to record health measurements, recognize changes, understand their significance, and prepare information for medical review.

Our Solution

ASTRA CARE provides a unified platform where astronauts can:

  • Monitor health: Record heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, sleep, mood, stress, symptoms, and activity context.
  • Analyze trends: Visualize historical observations and compare measurements against individual synthetic baselines.
  • Understand changes: Receive transparent, non-diagnostic assessments explaining observed values, calculated differences, possible interpretations, and suggested next steps.
  • Work offline: Save health records locally without requiring continuous Internet access.
  • Communicate with Earth: Generate structured health reports, queue them during simulated communication outages, and transmit them when connectivity becomes available.
  • Track report delivery: Verify report integrity using SHA-256 and record acknowledgements from a simulated ground medical receiver.

Technology Stack

ASTRA CARE was developed using Expo, React Native, React Native Web, Expo Router, and TypeScript, enabling shared mobile and web application development.

IndexedDB provides offline browser storage, while Expo SQLite supports local native data persistence. The simulated ground receiver uses Node.js, Fastify, and SQLite. The application uses deterministic baseline comparison algorithms, structured health observations, and explainable assessment logic.

Innovation

Our innovation lies in integrating astronaut self-monitoring, personalized baseline comparisons, transparent assessments, offline-first operation, and delay-tolerant medical reporting into one workflow.

Unlike a conventional health dashboard, ASTRA CARE demonstrates how medical observations can remain accessible onboard and be reliably transferred for review even when Earth communication is interrupted.

Impact and Benefits

ASTRA CARE aims to improve astronaut health awareness, reduce dependence on continuous Earth connectivity, and demonstrate how understandable, offline medical-support workflows could benefit future exploration missions.

The approach may also inspire remote healthcare applications for isolated communities on Earth.

Design Considerations

Our team prioritized usability for non-specialists, accessible interfaces, clear measurement units, scientific transparency, local data persistence, report integrity, communication delays, and appropriate medical safety boundaries.

The prototype uses fictional astronaut records and synthetic assessment rules. It does not diagnose medical conditions, prescribe treatments, or claim clinical validation or NASA flight certification.

ASTRA CARE demonstrates a practical foundation for future research into autonomous, crew-centered health monitoring.
